args.name: Place and arrange found material
args.function: Let me physically place an owned fallen branch on clear ground nearby, choosing its position and orientation to begin a small decorative arrangement. Inspect the actual material and placement constraints rather than assuming it can be shaped or joined.
args.conditions: I am outdoors near fallen branches on ordinary forest ground. I intend to collect one branch first. No tools, fasteners, shelter, or special material properties are established.
args.inputs: An actual owned branch and a reachable, unoccupied patch of ground; use only material actually supplied.
args.costs: Placement effort and time are unknown. The placed material must leave carried inventory and remain a real recoverable object, without duplication.
args.effects: A physically placed branch with its actual geometry and chosen orientation if feasible. No automatic happiness, safety, shelter, durability improvement, or mastery. Report infeasible placements rather than inventing success.

candidates.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-dug plot, where it may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect units, sites, plants and plot progress; cancel unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; stock still on a plant is not owned. x, y: a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Three paid rounds of 1 energy: loosen, place, cover; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Maintain: refused at no cost. Cancel: one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
candidates.effects: Loosening keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the open plot, where it cannot be eaten or used. Covering completes planting, not establishment: the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one, rooting only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 120 rounds, checks every 10; not a growth date. Maintain: no water transfer, amendment or hand-changeable obstruction exists. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Cancel, or death, before placing returns the unit once (where the person died); after placing, the unit stays uncovered, does not root and ages. No reward or refund.

candidates.function: Hum or sing a short quiet phrase with your own voice for 1-3 rounds; nearby people hear each voiced round.
candidates.costs: Study: 2 rounds at 0.2 energy each; each hums a short practice phrase heard nearby (silent in pain or distress). hum or sing: rounds 1-3 (default 1), 0.5 energy per voiced round, no material. phrase: 2-8 notes {pitch: -4..4 steps from the home note 0, beats: 1-4}, or improvise=true. sing may add text (at most 240 characters, as tell). Shared by study, hum and sing: at most 3 voiced rounds in any 10 rounds, and 2 unvoiced rounds after 3 voiced rounds in a row or in one bout; a start must fit every requested round. Checked at start and each round: alive; no pain (an injury in the last round) or distress (satiety 0, body temperature below 7 or above 34); at least 0.5 energy. A refused start or resume costs nothing. resume continues a paused bout after fresh checks; cancel takes one round and no energy; both use only mode.
candidates.effects: Each voiced round is one segment at your position: everyone else living within 5 units (tell's hearing radius), seen or not, gets a heard event and heard-list entry with your mode, phrase, words and segment. Silence, refusals and pauses are not heard. The sound ends with each segment; no object, item, mark or lasting sound is made. Another action, a refused round, too little energy, a limit, pain or distress pauses the bout without charge; voiced segments and their energy are never refunded. Death ends the bout and any study. improvise=true derives 4-6 notes from your id and the start round (FNV-1a and xorshift32; from 0, steps of -2..+2 within -3..+3, back to 0), never at random. No reward, mood change or practice milestone; listeners get only the heard entry, and no reaction is implied.

Existing drop (foundation-forest@1, forest.drop) transfers owned units to ground, but its complete schema accepts only target and quantity, not destination or orientation. Navigate, pickup and probe do not supply controlled spatial placement. Develop the missing positioning operation, reusing existing transfer and observation code rather than claiming those functions as new. Actual geometry, handling limits and ground clearance remain to be checked.\",\"specification\":\"Develop general capability 'Position loose material', parameterized by mode (inspect, place, inspect-progress, resume, cancel), target owned item ID, positive whole-unit quantity, destination world coordinates and orientation in radians. Apply to any actually hand-movable loose material, not just branches or this actor. First executable scope is one independently represented object at a time on reachable ground; no shaping, joining, fastening, elevated support or construction. Reject unsupported quantities without consuming them. Record code dependencies explicitly: reuse forest.drop's ownership, quantity conservation and transfer validation; existing pickup recovery, observation, spatial collision and work-lifecycle implementations where applicable. Do not change drop's contract or pretend it accepts positioning arguments. Implement the missing controlled-transform and persistent loose-object representation in the current-conversation development handoff. No world time passes while awaiting development/review.\\nReferences and prerequisites: target must resolve to an actual owned object at execution, initially item-128-sol-1488 (branch, quantity 1, origin canopy-74, harvestedAt 128); source canopy stock is not an input. Preserve target identity and provenance. Destination must be within the actor's established manual reach, inside bounds [48,36], on observed supportable ground, with the full represented object footprint clear of actors, obstacles and reservations. Revalidate ownership, reach, alive status, energy, handling capacity, geometry and clearance at execution; do not infer branch dimensions, straightness, mass, strength or joinability from its label or source-tree radius. Use existing authoritative geometry/material facts and directly observable inspection only. Where needed, add minimal coherent loose-object geometry and handling support to the implementation; do not silently invent favorable measurements. If necessary facts cannot be established, inspection reports them as unknown and placement remains unavailable for that target, with the missing mechanism retained in development rather than permanently rejecting the operation. No hidden stock or remote facts are revealed.\\nCosts and execution: standalone inspect costs one world round and 0.2 energy, no material, and reports only observable item and site constraints. Starting place performs the same paid inspection as stage 1, retaining exact item identity, requested transform, observations and remaining stage in a work record. Stage 2 takes one additional world round and 0.5 energy to move and orient the object; total successful new placement costs two rounds and 0.7 energy. Movement to the site is separate existing navigation with its actual costs. No tools, fasteners, water, heat or consumables are supplied. Insufficient energy or invalid prerequisites before a stage cause no stage charge; a paid inspection can return an informative infeasibility result without advancing to placement. Require sufficient real handling capacity; unsupported heavy or unwieldy materials need separately supplied assistance or equipment, not assumed strength.\\nConservation and products: until stage 2 commits, the item remains owned in carried inventory, ageing normally and unavailable to concurrent work. Atomically debit exactly the selected unit from carried inventory and move that same unit into a persistent recoverable ground object at the validated position and angle. Preserve quantity, material, condition, age and provenance, and retain the identity or an explicit one-to-one identity mapping if the engine requires a new representation. Never create both a carried unit and a ground copy. Do not merge spatially distinct placed objects into a stack that loses their transforms. Recovery uses existing pickup, with actual reach and its existing costs; subsequent repositioning requires actual recovery or a supported owned-ground-object move, not remote edits. A changed destination or orientation requires a fresh validated placement, not a free transform. Completion produces only the physically positioned object, not shelter, increased durability, safety, happiness or mastery.\\nProgress and lifecycle: stage records distinguish inspected, ready, paused, completed, infeasible and cancelled; record paid costs, input reference and committed output reference. Other actions, lost reach, temporary obstruction or insufficient energy pause before commitment. Resume rechecks live conditions and continues the unpaid stage; materially changed item or site requires a new paid inspection. Inspect-progress costs one round and 0.2 energy and reports existing work facts, not success by inference. Cancel takes one round, zero energy, releases any reservation once, and leaves an unplaced item in inventory; paid effort and elapsed time are never refunded. Death ends unfinished work and releases reservations, with the still-carried item handled once by existing death/inventory rules. Completed placements persist on cancellation, interruption or death. Atomic stage-2 failure neither debits inventory nor creates an object. Global review/development pauses advance neither work nor world processes.\\nOngoing behavior: placed items persist under applicable existing decay, weather, collision and collection rules; placement does not improve those properties. No autonomous arrangement, upkeep, regeneration or periodic material/energy debit is added. Reinspection and repositioning are actual paid actions if desired. Establish these validations, transactions and lifecycle rules in executable code, not repeated model approval.\",\"learning\":1,\"experienceReview\":\"Study requires one individual round at 0.2 energy after implementation is available; it grants only the learned operation, not an arranged object or mastery. No goals, budgets, permissions or protected reward balances are edited, and no other person's consent, participation or reaction is supplied.\",\"visualReview\":\"Emit observable inspection and work-state events containing actor, target, destination, requested angle, tick, stage, paid effort and explicit measured/unknown constraints.
